sovereign_country.strategic_role: 苏伊士运河经济特区、辐射中东及北非的低成本轻工制造

business_scope.primary_industry_name: Vertical Industrial ERP and Customer Relationship Software

meta_jurisdiction_context.legal_system_doctrine: Hybrid: Civil Law (French-model) with Islamic Sharia as the principal source of legislation per Article 2 of the 2014 Constitution; unitary national system without sub-state tax or corporate law differentiation
applicable_bilateral_investment_treaties: Agadir Agreement (2004, Egypt, Jordan, Morocco, Tunisia, PLO)
Treaty for the Promotion and Protection of Investment among Arab Countries (1980)

ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Law No. 80 of 2002 on Combating Money Laundering and Terrorist Financing, as amended by Law No. 36 of 2014 and substantially by Law No. 8 of 2022; Executive Regulations issued by Prime Ministerial Decree No. 954 of 2003 and subsequent amendments; Financial Regulatory Authority (FRA) Board Decree No. 30 of 2019 mandating the Beneficial Owner Register for all companies subject to FRA supervision; Central Bank of Egypt AML/CFT Rules issued under the Central Bank and Banking System Law No. 194 of 2020; Law No. 159 of 1981 (Companies Law); Law No. 72 of 2017 (Investment Law and its Executive Regulations by Presidential Decree No. 240 of 2018); Commercial Registry Law No. 34 of 1976; Law No. 94 of 2015 on Counter-Terrorism

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Notarized certified copy of the passport of each founding shareholder / beneficial owner (UBO)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Passport issuing authority in the shareholder's country of residence, verified by a licensed public notary
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Consular Legalization chain: Notary Public certification, then Ministry of Foreign Affairs of the issuing state, then Egyptian Embassy or Consulate in that state (Egypt is NOT a contracting party to the Hague Apostille Convention of 1961; apostilles are not accepted)

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Incumbency or Certificate of Good Standing for each corporate founding shareholder
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Registry of Companies / Companies House of the corporate shareholder's jurisdiction of incorporation
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Consular Legalization: corporate registry certification, then Ministry of Foreign Affairs of the issuing state, then Egyptian Embassy or Consulate; documents in a language other than Arabic or English require sworn translation after legalization

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Notarized Power of Attorney executed by all founders in favor of the local formation agent or resident manager
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Licensed public notary in the jurisdiction where each founder signs
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Consular Legalization chain: Notary Public, then Ministry of Foreign Affairs of the issuing state, then Egyptian Embassy or Consulate, then, after arrival in Egypt, Arabic sworn translation and registration at the Egyptian Notary Public (El-Shaher El-Adl)

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Memorandum of Association (Arabic draft) to be notarized by an Egyptian Notary Public (El-Shaher El-Adl)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Notary Public Department, Egyptian Ministry of Justice
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Internal notarization only; no consular legalization required for internally executed Egyptian instruments; the notarized Arabic MOA serves as the foundational incorporation deed

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Bank reference letter and signed source-of-funds declaration for each UBO with funds contributions
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Licensed deposit-taking bank in the UBO's country of residence
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Consular Legalization: bank certification and seal, then notarization, then Foreign Ministry of the issuing state, then Egyptian Embassy or Consulate; the letter must be issued within 90 days before filing

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory screening of all UBOs, shareholders, directors, and authorized signatories against the UN Consolidated Security Council Sanctions List, OFAC SDN List, EU Consolidated Financial Sanctions List, UK OFSI Consolidated List, and the Egyptian national terrorist list issued by the High Committee for Combating Terrorism pursuant to Law No. 94 of 2015; enhanced due diligence mandatory for PEPs, their family members, and close associates; negative news and adverse media checks across reputable global databases; continuous re-screening at minimum every 90 days; records retained for at least 5 years after the termination of the business relationship (or 10 years under certain FRA sectoral instructions), extended to 25 years for designated high-risk categories under the EMLCU directives; filing entity must confirm no direct or indirect association with designated persons or jurisdictions under FATF heightened monitoring.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: GAFI One-Stop-Shop Investor Services Portal administered by the General Authority for Investment and Free Zones (www.gafi.gov.eg); name clearance is executed electronically through the GAFI platform which interfaces with the Commercial Registry Database (El-Sijill El-Togary) supervised by the Egyptian Ministry of Supply and Internal Trade
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: The statutory name must be registered in Arabic characters. Arabic is the mandatory official language of the registry; a Latin-script transliteration may be added as the English trading name but has no legal effect on precedence. The name must include the legal form suffix in Arabic: 'شركة ذات مسئولية محدودة' or its accepted abbreviation 'ذ.م.م' meaning Limited Liability Company. The Arabic name must read from right to left, must be pronounceable in Arabic, and must not have a pernicious double meaning in either Arabic or English. The requested foreign-language name must be transliterated phonetically into Arabic script according to the standard phoneme mappings adopted by the Commercial Registry; the transliteration cannot depart from the approved Arabic phonetic root.
prohibited_and_sensitive_tokens: Bank, Banking, or any financial intermediation terms absent specific authorization by the Central Bank of Egypt
National, Government, Ministry, Presidency, Army, Police, Military, or Security
Arab Republic, Egypt, or geographically misleading tokens implying an official state body
Islamic, Sharia, Jihad, or religiously sensitive terms in a financial context
Foundation, Endowment, or Charitable fund absent official NGO registration
English terms such as 'Global', 'International', 'Group', or 'Holding' when the authorized capital and commercial scope do not support the representation
Any name identical or confusingly similar to a registered trademark, commercial title, or previously cleared company name
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: A rejected name may be challenged by filing a written grievance ('Tazallum') with the GAFI Investor Services Center within 30 calendar days from the rejection notification, attaching the name refusal letter, a new alternative name, and a supporting legal memorandum; GAFI must respond within 15 business days. If the internal grievance is denied, the founders may appeal to the Administrative Court of the Egyptian Council of State (Qada El-Adl El-Edari) within 60 days of the final administrative denial. A second refiling for a substantively identical or phonetically identical name, differing only in punctuation, diacritics, or the legal suffix, is barred and subject to administrative rejection. Filing a grievance tolls the expiry of the 30-day reservation window if the reservation has not yet lapsed.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Limited acceptance. Egyptian law requires every LLC to maintain a genuine, physical registered office within the jurisdiction where the statutory ledger, company seal, board minutes, and the notarized Memorandum of Association are kept and may be inspected by the Commercial Registry, GAFI, the Egyptian Tax Authority, and the Social Insurance Authority. For the vertical cloud ERP/CRM software business segment, GAFI practice accepts a qualifying virtual-office arrangement provided that: (a) the virtual office promoter holds a physical lease of at least 8 square meters of dedicated commercial space in an office-rated building; (b) a resident office manager maintains custody of the statutory records and receives service of legal process; (c) the company name is displayed at the entrance panel; and (d) no e-commerce-only designation is used that would exclude the physical address from the commercial registry. A pure desk-service with no resident agent and no dedicated address will be refused by the Commercial Registry and will trigger automatic deferral of the incorporation file.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Moderate risk of approximately 25% probability of an unannounced physical inspection by GAFI or the Egyptian Tax Authority within the first 12 months of incorporation for a foreign-owned cloud-SaaS LG; probability escalates to 65% if the company's tax file shows zero local payroll, zero local procurement, or if the registered office address is shared with more than 5 unrelated companies; probability reduces to below 10% when the company maintains a qualified resident office manager, displays signage, and maintains localized contracts with third-party data processors within Egypt.

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Name clearance search and 30-day reservation administrative fee
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: GAFI / Commercial Registry of the Ministry of Supply and Internal Trade
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Ministerial tariff schedule under Commercial Registry Law No. 34 of 1976; approximate statutory fee EGP 750 (approx. USD 15) covering one name search and 30 days of reservation

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Notarization of the Arabic Memorandum of Association and companion incorporation instruments by El-Shaher El-Adl (Egyptian Notary Public)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Notary Public Department, Egyptian Ministry of Justice
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Notary Tariff issued under Law No. 108 of 2000; fee band for commercial incorporation deeds of EGP 5,500 - 6,000 (approx. USD 115) including proportional stamp duty components based on a nominal nominal authorized capital not exceeding EGP 100,000

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Sworn English-Arabic certified translation of the MOA, POA, and UBO identification documents (estimated 15 pages)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Sworn Translation Office licensed by the Egyptian Supreme Council for Culture
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Prevailing market benchmark of EGP 400 - 600 per page (approx. USD 8 - 12), totaling approximately EGP 7,200 (approx. USD 145) for the full instrument set inclusive of translator's seal and declaratory rider

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Commercial Registry certificate issuance and mandatory one-time publication of the formation announcement in the Official Gazette (Al-Waqa'i Al-Masriya)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Commercial Registry and the Official Gazette (Government Press)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Combined statutory tariff under Law No. 159 of 1981 and Law No. 72 of 2017 of EGP 4,000 - 5,000 (approx. USD 90) covering the commercial certificate, documents ledger, and publication duty

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: GAFI incorporation file opening, investment file processing, and one-stop-shop administrative fee
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: General Authority for Investment and Free Zones (GAFI)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Investment Law No. 72 of 2017 tariff; standard incorporation processing fee of EGP 8,500 (approx. USD 170) inclusive of investor services basket, digital file token, and technical attach proof issuance

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Consular legalization of foreign UBO and corporate documents (passport copies, certificate of incumbency, bank reference letters, POA - approximately 4 documents)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Egyptian Ministry of Foreign Affairs and the Egyptian Embassy/Consulate in the issuing jurisdiction
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Consular fee schedule published by the Egyptian Ministry of Foreign Affairs; standard per-document fee of EGP 1,500 - 3,500, with an average of EGP 2,500 per document, totaling approximately EGP 12,000 (approx. USD 240) excluding courier costs

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Registered office and qualifying virtual-office arrangement - first 12-month lease and resident office manager services
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Licensed commercial formation agent and facility lease counterparty
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Prevailing Greater Cairo commercial market rate of USD 90 - 120 per month for an 8 sqm registered office package with resident office manager, annualized at USD 1,200

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Stage-1 AML/CFT UBO comply-file compilation (PEP and sanctions screening reports, UBO declarations, retention scheduling, internal compliance memo)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: External AML compliance counsel engaged by the founders
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Prevailing market fixed fee of USD 200 - 250 for low-risk non-banking cloud technology entities, inclusive of EDG screenings across UN, OFAC, EU, UK and Egyptian national lists, and the 25% UBO ownership threshold declaration set

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Contingency buffer for name rejection grievance and refiling (administrative appeal fee and counsel drafting time)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: GAFI / Ministry of Justice and external legal counsel
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Contingency provisioning: 2x base name-filing fee (approx. USD 30) plus 30 minutes of legal drafting time at a blended rate of USD 60 per half-hour, totaling USD 60

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Companies Law No. 159 of 1981 on Joint-Stock Companies, Partnerships Limited by Shares and Limited Liability Companies, as amended by Law No. 4 of 2009 and Law No. 139 of 2019 (LLC provisions: Arts. 102-114; incorporation procedures: Arts. 14-17); Investment Law No. 72 of 2017 and Executive Regulations issued by Prime Ministerial Decree No. 2310 of 2017; VAT Law No. 67 of 2016 for fiscal registration. An LLC may not offer its quotas to the public.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: General Authority for Investment and Free Zones (GAFI) - Investment Services Center (One-Stop-Shop) and GAFI Commercial Registration Offices; notarial authentication performed by the Real Estate Registration and Notarization Authority (Ministry of Justice) co-located at the One-Stop-Shop.
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Incorporation Contract (Aqd Al-Ta'sis) containing the Articles of Association, filed via the GAFI E-Services / Invest in Egypt online portal and authenticated by a licensed Egyptian notary before commercial registration.
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum paid-up capital applies to an Egyptian LLC; the founders freely fix the capital which must be fully subscribed at formation, divided into equal quotas with a nominal value of not less than EGP 100 each (Art. 103, Law 159/1981). Cash subscriptions must be deposited in a bank account of the company-under-formation and evidenced by a bank certificate; in-kind contributions require a certified valuation by a registered accountant. No escrow-hold or freeze requirement applies to software service activities (ISIC 6201); capital may be used immediately after registration for operational expenses.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: PRO-FORMA FIRST BOARD RESOLUTION OF [COMPANY] LLC — Adopted by the founding managers on the incorporation date under Law No. 159 of 1981, as amended. RESOLVED: (1) the incorporation contract is ratified and the subscribed quotas are fully allotted to the founding partners; (2) the registered office shall be the address stated in the contract; (3) [Name] is appointed General Manager and [Name] is appointed Company Secretary, each authorized to open and operate bank accounts, execute contracts, and represent the company before GAFI, the tax authority, and all public bodies; (4) the General Manager shall e-file statutory documents and pay all incorporation fees.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Trade Name Reservation and Legal Form Pre-Check
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: GAFI Commercial Registration Department - online via GAFI E-Services portal and Invest in Egypt website
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Log in to the GAFI e-portal or attend the One-Stop-Shop counter; file an e-application containing three Arabic candidate trade names, the intended object clause (vertical ERP/CRM software development, hosted cloud services, software licensing, and consultancy), and the proposed LLC legal form; pay the name reservation fee (approx. EGP 100) via Fawry or state e-payment gateway; the system issues a name availability report and reserves the accepted name for 60 days.
required_dossiers: Copy of national ID or passport of each founding partner
Notarized power of attorney if a founder acts by proxy
Three alternative trade names in Arabic and Latin script
Preliminary indication of the registered office address (optional at this step)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the name is refused for similarity with an existing mark, the registry will identify the conflicting entry; re-file with three new alternatives within five business days; a contested refusal may be escalated to the GAFI legal complaints unit within ten days.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Notary Office of the Real Estate Registration and Notarization Authority (Ministry of Justice), co-located with the GAFI One-Stop-Shop
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Prepare the Arabic incorporation contract setting out capacity, object, capital, quota division, registered office, management rules, and first managers; obtain a bank certificate of the deposit of cash subscriptions into the company-under-formation account, or an in-kind valuation certificate signed by a registered accountant; appear before the notary with all founders or their lawful proxies to authenticate signatures; the notary stamps and numbers the contract and transmits the authenticated copy electronically to the GAFI registration system.
required_dossiers: Draft incorporation contract and articles of association in Arabic
GAFI name reservation certificate
Copy of national ID or passport of each founder
Power of attorney if a proxy signs
Original bank capital deposit certificate or certified in-kind valuation report
Lease agreement or preliminary title for the registered office
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the notary flags a deficiency, such as a quota value below EGP 100 or an invalid legal capacity, amend the contract and re-authenticate the corrected pages within the same working day; a valuation objection may be cured by submitting an updated certificate from a registered accountant.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: GAFI E-Filing, Commercial Registration, and Unified Tax Number Issuance
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: GAFI Investment Services Center (One-Stop-Shop) intake window and e-payment portal
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: File the complete post-notarization package through the GAFI One-Stop-Shop e-intake; the registry officer verifies the contract against Law 159/1981 Arts. 103-114 and the Investment Law, collects the state fees (commercial registration fee, electronic gazette fee, and service charges), and issues the Commercial Registration Extract; the company's Unified Tax Number is automatically registered with the Egyptian Tax Authority through the integrated tax window and appears on the final acceptance notice.
required_dossiers: Notarized incorporation contract (original)
GAFI name reservation certificate
Bank capital deposit certificate or in-kind valuation certificate
Certified lease contract and landlord title deed for the registered office
Unified tax number Annex form (pre-filled by GAFI)
Proof of state fee payment via Fawry or e-payment gateway
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the authority issues a pending-papers notice, the applicant has 15 days to complete the file; if registration is refused on legal grounds, file an objection with the GAFI Dispute Settlement Committee within 60 days under Law 72 of 2017, and thereafter appeal to the Administrative Court (Council of State) within 60 days.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Official Gazette Publication of the Incorporation Summary
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Official Gazette and Al-Waqa'i Al-Masriya printing house (government press)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit an abstract of the incorporation contract containing the corporate name, object, capital, quota structure, and managers, together with the commercial registration number; pay the publication fee, which is calculated per column, and obtain the gazette issue containing the notice; publication constitutes legal notice to third parties and is a precondition for enforceability against bona fide third parties.
required_dossiers: Signed abstract of the incorporation contract in Arabic
Commercial Registration Extract
Unified Tax Number certificate
Gazette publication fee receipt
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the gazette prints an error in the abstract, file a corrective notice request with the reduced correction fee; if the submission is misplaced, request a duplicate gazette issue by presenting the original fee receipt.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Tax Registration, E-Invoicing Enrollment, and VAT Profile
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Egyptian Tax Authority (ETA) - integrated GAFI window and ETA e-services and e-invoicing portals
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Confirm the automatically assigned Unified Tax Number with the ETA and obtain the official tax card; register for VAT under Law 67 of 2016, noting the mandatory registration threshold of EGP 500,000 in annual taxable supplies, and recommend voluntary registration for the B2B ERP/CRM cloud business; enroll in the ETA e-invoicing platform and obtain the company e-invoice and e-receipt cryptographic keys for compliant issuance to Egyptian clients; complete salary tax registration and Form 41 payroll setup before the first payroll run.
required_dossiers: Commercial Registration Extract
Unified Tax Number certificate
Articles of association and incorporation contract
Lease contract and civil defense certificate (for premises inspection)
Authorized financial signatory national ID
Bank account certificate evidencing capital deposit
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Unified Tax Number is not reflected within 72 hours, open an ETA service-window request attaching the GAFI acceptance receipt; if e-invoicing enrollment fails at the technical stage, file an ETA support ticket and re-issue the certificates; any dispute on tax obligation is settled through the ETA internal objection procedure.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Corporate Bank Account Opening and Social Insurance Activation
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Licensed Egyptian commercial bank and the National Organization for Social Insurance (NOSI)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Open a corporate settlement account at a licensed Egyptian bank (e.g., CIB, Bank of Alexandria, or QNB Alahli) presenting the incorporation package and the board resolution; the bank applies standard KYC and ultimate beneficial owner (UBO) due diligence, with no local shareholder restriction as non-resident ownership of an LLC is permitted; register the employer file with NOSI, obtain the employer social insurance number, and enroll the first employees; after receiving the IBAN, configure the international payment rails (Stripe Billing and Direct Debit) for subscription collections.
required_dossiers: Commercial Register Extract and tax card
Notarized first board resolution appointing signatories
Passport or national ID copies and UBO declaration of all shareholders
Bank KYC account application forms
NOSI employer registration form and lease contract
Specimen signature cards and company stamp
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the bank requires enhanced due diligence on a pre-revenue entity, provide a statutory declaration of source of funds and the GAFI licensed-activity certificate; if NOSI identifies discrepancies in employee data, amend the payroll schedule and re-submit within ten working days.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Industrial Development Authority (IDA) - clearance not applicable to ISIC 6201 (software and cloud services); the activity is non-facility-based and requires no IDA industrial license and no NTRA operating permit under Telecommunications Regulation Law No. 10 of 2003.
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Commercial Registration Extract and Unified Tax Number Cards serve as the general operating license of the LLC; a separate sectoral license is not required for vertical ERP/CRM cloud software provisioning.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Egyptian Environmental Affairs Agency (EEAA) - Ministry of Environment
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Category C (registration / exemption tier) under the Executive Regulations of Environmental Law No. 4 of 1994, as amended by Law No. 9 of 2009; an office-based software activity files a short EIA screening form and no Full EIA Report is required in the absence of manufacturing, fuel combustion, or hazardous materials.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Sanitary sewage discharged to the municipal network per Decree No. 92 of 2013 standards; no industrial wastewater or VOC point-source emissions are generated; any standby diesel generator must comply with Law No. 4 of 1994 air emission limits; e-waste and ICT hardware must be handed to EEAA-licensed recyclers under the national WEEE framework; office interiors must meet occupational VOC exposure thresholds.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Fire safety certificate issued by the General Administration of Civil Defense (Ministry of Interior) for the leased office floor, confirming egress routes and extinguishing systems; structural load inspection by a licensed civil engineer for server and equipment rooms; electrical installation inspection certificate; occupational safety and health clearance under Labor Law No. 12 of 2003 (Arts. 221-228) covering ventilation, emergency lighting, and first aid; third-party liability and fire insurance endorsed.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Egyptian Tax Authority (ETA), Ministry of Finance; official e-portal: www.eta.gov.eg; mandatory e-invoicing integration via the ETA Raman platform (invoicing.eta.gov.eg)
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: The foreign parent must (1) incorporate the Egyptian Limited Liability Company through the General Authority for Investment and Free Zones (GAFI) one-stop-shop and obtain the Commercial Register certificate; (2) file the tax registration application with the ETA within 30 days of incorporation, appointing a locally resident tax representative; (3) obtain the Unified Tax Card bearing the 14-digit Tax Identification Number (TIN) and tax file number; (4) register for VAT in the same tax file when taxable supplies meet or are expected to meet the EGP 500,000 annual threshold or opt for voluntary VAT registration to recover input VAT; and (5) enroll in the ETA e-invoicing system to obtain the digital certificate, API credentials, and billing entity ID.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.default_entity_tax_classification: Entity_Level_Taxation: the LLC is a resident juridical person subject to corporate income tax on worldwide income at 22.5% under Law No. 91 of 2005; no fiscal transparency or pass-through status exists; dividends to non-resident shareholders attract 10% domestic withholding tax, subject to treaty relief; Suez Canal Economic Zone and Free Zone entities may elect special regimes.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: Egyptian law does not provide a check-the-box or hybrid-mismatch flow-through election; the LLC is mandatorily an entity-level taxpayer. Available statutory elections: (a) Investment Law No. 72 of 2017 tax incentive election allowing an annual deduction of 30% to 50% of invested capital for up to 7 years for certified software/IT projects; (b) Special Economic Zone election under the SCZone authority providing a simplified 0% customs and reduced-rate corporate income tax regime; (c) Free Zone election replacing standard CIT and VAT with a flat annual 1% levy on proceeds for qualifying goods activities, generally unsuitable for domestic cloud services; (d) voluntary VAT registration election enabling input VAT recovery and export zero-rating claims.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: Value Added Tax (VAT) under Law No. 67 of 2016, as amended by Law No. 3 of 2021 and subsequent ministerial decrees
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: EGP 500,000 of annual taxable turnover in goods and services per calendar year; voluntary registration is permitted below the threshold, and registration is mandatory for any foreign entity whose Egyptian taxable supplies exceed this threshold
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Mandatory e-invoicing and e-receipts under Prime Ministerial Decree No. 265 of 2020; every registered taxpayer above the phased turnover requirements must issue invoices through certified billing software integrated via API with the ETA Raman platform in XML/JSON format; each invoice is cleared in near-real time and receives a unique UUID and machine-readable QR code before legal validity; the digital stamping requirement applies to export invoices as well as domestic sales; non-clearance renders the invoice inadmissible for input VAT deduction and export refund purposes.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Zero-rating is available for export of goods and certain international services. For the ISIC 6201 vertical cloud software/CRM service, the exporter must demonstrate: (a) the recipient is a non-resident customer located outside Egypt; (b) the place of supply and beneficial use of the software occurs wholly outside Egypt, applying the 'use and enjoyment' test; (c) consideration is received in foreign currency through a licensed Egyptian bank; and (d) no part of the service is consumed in Egypt or contributes to Egyptian-source income. The export sale invoice must carry the ETA-cleared UUID/QR code, and the related input VAT may be claimed as a refund or offset after documentary verification.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration (automated NAFEZA single-window clearance record)
Bill of Lading or Airway Bill evidencing physical export movement (where applicable)
Commercial invoice issued at 0% VAT referencing the ETA e-invoice UUID and QR code
Signed service contract with the non-resident customer defining destination and use
Foreign currency inward remittance certificate issued by the Egyptian bank
ETA-cleared e-invoice XML/JSON export file from the Raman platform
Evidence of corporate tax file registration and valid Unified Tax Card
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: The ETA may audit export zero-rating claims within the 5-year statutory prescription period and retrospectively claw back the unapplied 14% VAT on the export value together with delay interest of 1% per month where the documentary bundle is incomplete, the foreign-currency remittance is not timely repatriated, or the service is found to be consumed in Egypt. Forgery, false declarations, or fictitious export documents expose the taxpayer to criminal prosecution under Articles 34 and 80 of Law No. 67 of 2016 with imprisonment of up to 5 years and fines of EGP 20,000 to EGP 100,000, in addition to disgorgement of all refunded amounts, administrative penalties, and inclusion on the ETA high-risk compliance register, which suspends e-invoice clearance and access to export incentive facilities.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: The Egyptian Pound (EGP) is largely convertible for current account transactions, including trade settlements and profit remittances, subject to submission of supporting documentation to an authorized bank. Capital account transactions remain subject to CBE approval or post-transaction verification, with foreign direct investment repatriation generally permitted through authorized channels upon presentation of audited financial statements, tax clearance, and bank attestations. Profit remittances of Egyptian LLCs to non-resident shareholders are permitted via local banks against certified financials, annual audited accounts, and tax compliance certificates. No separate repatriation or profit remittance license is required for standard distribution, but banks apply strict beneficial ownership and source-of-funds checks.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: Export proceeds must be repatriated to an Egyptian licensed bank within 90 days from the date of shipment under CBE regulations. There is no mandatory percentage conversion into EGP currently; exporters retain the right to hold foreign currency proceeds in retention accounts. However, banks are obligated to ensure receipt of proceeds within the statutory window, and any extension must be approved by the CBE. Failure to comply may attract administrative penalties or suspension of import privileges.

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Offshore digital EMI cross-border viability is Low. Foreign or non-bank digital EMI suppliers are not permitted to open EGP current accounts or receive deposits on behalf of Egyptian entities without a local payment-service license from the CBE. Licensed local fintech players (e.g., Paymob, Fawry) may act as payment gateways and collection agents but cannot substitute for a full corporate banking relationship for trade settlement or capital remittance. An Egyptian LLC must maintain a local corporate account with a CBE-qualified bank for statutory capital, trade, and tax obligations.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Physical presence of at least one authorized director, and in most cases all board signatories, is mandated for original signature verification and biometric capture during the corporate account opening process. Remote opening is not generally permitted for LLCs under the CBE AML/CFT framework; video-conference KYC is accepted only as a supplementary measure and never as a substitute for the physical branch visit. For foreign shareholders holding more than 25%, a local authorized representative with notarized power of attorney and certified passport copies is required; original corporate documents apostilled or notarized to Egyptian consular standards are needed.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Uncertainty over ultimate beneficial owner identity or non-transparent ownership chain for the Egyptian LLC, especially with non-resident shareholders in high-risk jurisdictions.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: UBO declaration form, a written ownership chain of all direct and indirect shareholders up to natural persons, certified passport copies, notarized articles of association, board resolutions, valid national ID of the local manager, and audited bank reference letters from each shareholder's corporate bank.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Missing verifiable source of funds for the initial capital injection or excluded sanctions-list screening results.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Board-approved capital contribution notice, signed subscription agreement, bank-to-bank reference confirming source of funds, source-of-wealth statement, dividend payment evidence from previous profitable entities, and a negative sanctions screening report from a recognized provider (Refinitiv / Dow Jones / sonovate).

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Trade operations mismatch: invoice amounts higher than revenue capacity or prematurely reported operational expenses while capital is still being escrowed.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: The latest annual/audited financial statements (if any), an initial cash-flow projection for the ERP-Cloud vertical, signed master SaaS subscription contracts, ordinary course of business justification for outbound disbursements, and custom invoices showing standard software licensing / CRM hosting charges.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Residence and business premise verification failure in the absence of a physical office or on-site visit.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Valid commercial registration, tax card, electricity invoice, lease agreement under the LLC's name, official address photo, authorized third-party notarized lease approval from the building owner, and court-issued address verification if needed.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Exposure to sanctioned persons, dual-use software or cloud infrastructure that may trigger export-control review.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: For each counterparty: full legal name, nationality, industry classification, end-user certificate stating legitimate ERP / CRM usage for enterprise management, license agreements with clear permitted-use clauses, system audit logs, and assurance from the cloud provider that data is hosted on non-sanctioned servers with export-controlled data not involved.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Inbound foreign capital injections must be wired via SWIFT MT103 from the shareholder's overseas bank to the LLC's Capital Escrow Account at a CBE-licensed bank. The wire must reference the correct purpose code and a description such as 'INVESTMENT CAPITAL CONTRIBUTION' or 'SHARE CAPITAL SUBSCRIPTION.' The receiving bank will verify the source of funds, the underlying investment committee resolution, and the LLC's capital documents. The bank posts the EGP equivalent or retains the foreign currency, whichever was applied for at the time of conversion, and issues a bank currency conversion slip if conversion is required. Post-transfer compliance includes submitting a capital contribution settlement letter, an EGP foreign currency account statement, and registration of foreign investment through the General Authority for Investment (GAFI), if applicable.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Operating outbound disbursements for trade settlements and SaaS-related vendor payments use standard SWIFT MT103 payment instructions via the LLC's operational bank. For larger procurement of licences, hardware infrastructure or cross-border data services, the bank may require a Commercial Letter of Credit (LC) where the beneficiary is a foreign supplier requesting guaranteed payment; in such cases the operative rail is a documentary sight LC issued on the LLC's bank through a corresponding international bank. Direct debit is permissible only for domestic service billing (telecom, utilities and software charges), and for cross-border recurring payments the LLC should establish ACH or SEPA rails from its foreign subsidiary, if any, or utilise a licensed local payment aggregator only for collection from Egyptian clients. All outbound wires must be mapped to the appropriate SIMAD customs code or CBE payment code, and invoices must be retained for tax audit.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Egyptian banks may provide spot and forward (up to 12 months) foreign exchange contracts for genuine trade and capital accounts having sufficient underlying exposure; such forwards require a clear commercial transaction or service compulsion.

Non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) are not generally permitted by Egyptian licensed banks for hedging EGP, as onshore markets disallow offshore NDF settlement; the CBE prefers outright deliverable forwards for EGP exposures.
Currency swaps are permissible only when used to offset a matched cross-border trade flow, with bank approval and strict underlying documentation.
Reverse repo structures are not permitted for hedge purposes; simple FX swaps between EGP and USD/EUR are only licensed after documenting the economic need and maintaining active trade evidence.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Commercial Register annual renewal confirmation and fee payment
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: GAFI One-Stop Shop / Commercial Registry (Ministry of Trade and Industry)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annually, during the calendar month of the company's registration anniversary; online payment must clear before the last business day of that month.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late fee of EGP 100–500 per month per GAFI schedule; suspension of commercial-register extracts and notarization services; administrative strike-off from the register if unpaid for 12 consecutive months.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Audited annual financial statements, manager's report, and statutory audit report deposited with the Commercial Registry
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Fiscal year ending 31 December: annual partners' assembly by 30 June; audited statements deposited with the Commercial Registry immediately after assembly approval and no later than 30 June.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Fine of EGP 10,000–1,000,000 for responsible managers under Companies Law No. 1 of 2022; blocking of all registry extracts; persistent default triggers administrative strike-off.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual UBO (beneficial-ownership) register confirmation and declaration update
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: GAFI / Commercial Registry (centralized national beneficial-ownership database accessible by the Egyptian AML and Terrorist Financing Combating Unit)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annually together with the Commercial Register renewal in the registration-anniversary month, and within 15 days of any change in direct or indirect ownership, voting, or management control.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Fine of EGP 100,000–2,000,000 under the amended AML Law No. 80 of 2002 for failure to declare or for a materially inaccurate declaration; repetition exposes the entity to registration suspension and strike-off.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual corporate income tax return (ETA digital e-filing)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within four months of the tax year end; for a 31 December tax year the statutory filing deadline is 30 April of the following year, with ETA e-filing practice admitting returns until 31 May.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late-filing penalty of 2% per month on the assessed tax (maximum 100% of the tax), monthly delay interest, revocation of the tax clearance certificate required for banking and notarial operations, and ETA embargo measures.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Notarized annual partners' assembly minutes and dividend or profit-appropriation endorsement
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: GAFI Notarial Directorate / Notary Public and the Commercial Registry
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: No later than 30 June following the fiscal year end; the minutes entry in the company's minute book must be notarized, and a certified copy deposited with the Commercial Registry together with the audited financial statements.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Managers face the Companies Law fine regime of EGP 10,000–1,000,000 and civil liability for any unverified or unlawful distribution of profits to partners.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: All Egyptian LLCs, including the ISIC 6201 cloud-software entity, must appoint at least one certified auditor registered on the Financial Regulatory Authority auditor list. There is no revenue or asset exemption under Companies Law No. 1 of 2022, and the capital-based dispensation of the old Law No. 159 of 1981 no longer applies.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Egyptian Accounting Standards (EAS), a statutory local GAAP materially converged with IFRS; consolidated group parents may apply full IFRS at group level, while the Egyptian stand-alone statutory financial statements are drawn up under EAS in Arabic.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: The LLC must maintain a register of beneficial owners identifying every natural person directly or indirectly controlling more than 10% of the capital, votes, or management, and must re-affirm that register through GAFI's Companies Online Services at each annual Commercial Register renewal. LLC share transfers require transfer formalities under the Articles of Association and commercial re-registration; on any contract- or stake-transfer event the UBO data must be re-declared within 15 days and again at the next annual renewal even if the shareholding remains unchanged.

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: USD 150–600 per year for a Cairo or Giza registered-address and licensed administrative agent package; premium serviced offices in the New Administrative Capital are higher.
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: USD 1,500–5,000 per fiscal year for a small vertical-cloud LLC with stand-alone EAS financial statements and one legal-entity audit.

corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: No automatic software-sector tax holiday is granted under the Egyptian Income Tax Law. Qualifying investments under Investment Law No. 72 of 2017 may benefit from a reduced CIT rate of 50% for 5 years in certain strategic zones; companies operating exclusively from an approved Free Zone under Law 72/2017 are generally exempt from Egyptian corporate income tax on export-oriented activity, subject to meeting registered activity and economic-substance conditions. Cloud/ERP software publishing (ISIC 6201) is not per se listed as a Free Zone activity and requires an explicit Free Zone licence to invoke the exemption.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Egyptian Corporate Income Tax Return (Form No. 16) filed electronically through the Egyptian Tax Authority's e-Tax Portal (www.eta.gov.eg); the single unified return procedure also integrates any required transfer-pricing disclosure schedules.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.reporting_frequency: Annual; advance CIT instalments are payable in two or more instalments during the fiscal year under the Tax Procedures Law, with the annual return serving as the final reconciliation.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: The annual CIT return must be filed no later than four months after the end of the fiscal year (for a calendar-year entity, by 30 April). The ETA may extend the deadline on a justified application, but extension does not suspend the accrual of late-payment penalties.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Taxpayer identification: commercial register number, tax card number, legal form (Limited Liability Company), fiscal year-end, and registered address.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: A non-resident entity deriving Egyptian-source income through a branch or deemed permanent establishment must enter the Egyptian branch registration number and appoint an authorised fiscal representative before return submission.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Residence classification: resident legal entity (incorporated in Egypt or central management in Egypt) versus non-resident foreign enterprise with a permanent establishment in Egypt.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Classify the filer as a non-resident and indicate whether a PE exists under Egyptian domestic law and the applicable tax treaty; remote server or cloud-hosting infrastructure is not automatically accepted as a PE and must be analysed on facts.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Principal business activity code: ISIC 6201 (computer programming / software publishing) and commercial model description: subscription, ERP, CRM, cloud/SaaS, support and professional services.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Use activity code 6201 and describe Egyptian-source revenue, whether attributable to any branch activity, and any DTA allocation of business profits.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Gross revenue: total turnover from Egyptian and foreign sources, separately identifying subscription licence fees, SaaS hosting revenue, support fees, and any incidental sale of software.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Enter only Egyptian-source revenue attributable to the PE or to the application of the PE attribution rules; do not consolidate worldwide revenue unless there is a full Egyptian PE.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Deductible expenses: direct costs of software development, cloud hosting, amortisation of capitalised intangible assets, salaries, rental, marketing, and administrative overhead; non-deductible items include penalties, personal costs and certain taxes.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Enter only expenses apportioned to the Egyptian PE, supported by transfer-pricing documentation and intercompany allocation records; tie to the local file profit and loss statement.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Net taxable income after applying statutory deductions and losses carried forward. Egyptian tax losses may be used to reduce future taxable profits for a maximum of five years.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Report PE-only net profit; losses incurred outside Egypt by the foreign head office cannot be used against Egyptian PE profit.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Tax computation and applicable CIT rate: 22.5% for resident LLCs and foreign PEs; any Free Zone or investment-law preferential rate must be supported by a valid tax facility letter.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Compute 22.5% on PE-allocated taxable income; confirm whether any 5% branch-remittance tax or treaty alternative applies to profits remitted after tax.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Reliefs and credits: double-taxation treaty relief, foreign tax credits, advance or provisional CIT paid during the year, and any withholding taxes already borne on Egyptian-source income.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Attach the current Tax Residency Certificate from the home-state authority, the DTA relief application approval, and reconciliation of withholding tax certificates received from Egyptian counterparties.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Final liability or refund: net CIT due after advance payments, or the refundable amount, and designation of the Egyptian payment channel or designated local bank account.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident filers should instruct payment from an Egyptian bank account via ETA e-payment; refund requests require verified tax refund procedure and bank-transfer instruction.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing attracts a fixed civil fine plus a statutory monthly surcharge calculated on the unpaid tax for each month of delay, subject to a maximum cap, and a daily non-compliance surcharge may be imposed under the Tax Procedures Law No. 188 of 2020 when the taxpayer fails to respond to official notification. Intentional non-filing or fraudulent under-declaration triggers criminal fines up to twice the evaded tax and imprisonment. Late payment also blocks issuance of the tax clearance certificate required for dividend repatriation and for commercial registration renewal.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 10% domestic withholding tax on dividends and profit distributions made by an Egyptian LLC to its shareholders, whether resident or non-resident, unless a lower treaty rate applies or the recipient is subject to a participation-exemption or Free Zone licence privilege. The distribution of distributable reserves, capital-reduction distributions, and liquidation surpluses may be characterised as dividends and taxed at 10% to the extent of accumulated profits.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: To invoke treaty relief, the non-resident shareholder must file a DTA relief application with the Egyptian Tax Authority before the distribution date, attaching a Tax Residency Certificate (TRC) issued by the tax authority of the shareholder's jurisdiction, legalisation or apostille required for non-GCC countries unless exempt, a beneficial-ownership declaration, and the actual shareholding records. For branch profit remittance, the foreign taxpayer must apply for the lower treaty rate on the 5% branch-repatriation tax; the ETA generally issues a written approval after examining the treaty, PE attribution, and Turkish? Not Turkish; after examining the treaty and financial statements; the reduced rate is enforced at source only after approval, otherwise a refund claim may be filed using the ordinary tax-refund mechanism.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Domestic Egyptian law imposes a 20% withholding tax on royalty payments and a 20% withholding tax on interest paid to non-residents. Treaty rates commonly reduce royalties to 10%–15% and interest to 10%–15%, conditional on beneficial ownership and substantive DTA relief. SaaS/cloud licensing payments are evaluated under Egyptian tax law and the relevant DTA to determine whether they are royalties for the use of copyright/IP, technical-service business profits, or PE-attributable revenues; where the non-resident has no Egyptian PE and no DTA, the gross-royalty tax of 20% is generally withheld by the local payer.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: EGP 5,000,000 aggregate annual related-party transactions for preparing and submitting the Egyptian Local File; EGP 50,000,000 group-related turnover for the consolidated Egyptian Master File; a transfer-pricing disclosure schedule is required for related-party transactions exceeding EGP 1,000,000, and non-resident cost-sharing or intercompany service charges must be supported by economic analysis and CUP benchmarking records.
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: Egypt does not administer a separate UAE-style Economic Substance Regulations regime; however, the Egyptian Tax Authority applies general anti-avoidance rules under Law 91/2005 and Tax Procedures Law 188/2020 that disregard transactions lacking commercial purpose. Free Zone companies must retain real physical presence, employees and activity to preserve their CIT exemption. Controlled-foreign-company rules and the permanent-establishment allocation rules operate as functional economic-substance requirements for software companies entering and exiting Egypt.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Deliberate concealment of Egyptian-source revenue, use of a foreign cloud invoicing vehicle to route local subscriptions outside Egypt, fabrication of deductible expenses, or submission of forged VAT or withholding-tax invoices to reduce CIT.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Criminal conviction under Law 91/2005 as amended carries imprisonment for not less than one year and up to five years, a fine equal to 100%–200% of the evaded tax, and a further civil tax assessment at double the unpaid amount. Understating revenue by more than 30% is treated as prima facie fraud and disables the taxpayer from utilising a clearance certificate.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors, managers, and authorised signatories who execute or assist in the evasion scheme are jointly and severally liable for the unpaid tax and the fraud fine. Egyptian courts may pierce the LLC veil when corporate funds are used for personal purposes or the company is operated as a facade; civil asset attachment, travel bans, and confiscation of personal property are available against culpable directors.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Forming or using an Egyptian LLC as a letterbox entity with no real commercial function, staffing, office, or decision-making, solely to receive global ERP/CRM cloud revenue, obtain a Free Zone exemption or a treaty residence certificate, and then remit profits to an ultimate principal without arm's-length remuneration.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: The ETA has authority to disregard the interposed entity and reallocate taxable income to the real owner under the anti-avoidance rules; the purported free-zone exemption is revoked retroactively, WHT of 10% is imposed on all repatriated profits, and a penalty of up to 100% of the uncovered tax may apply. Criminal penalties for sham invoicing and false declarations may be imposed under the Penal Code.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Nominee directors and legal representatives can be held personally liable for unpaid taxes when the company is a pure conduit and corporate assets were intermingled with the principal's assets. Travel bans, freezing orders, and disqualification from serving on Egyptian companies are routinely issued; imprisonment is possible for knowingly executing sham transactions.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Accepting recurring cloud-subscription payments via Stripe Billing or direct debit from customers whose beneficial-ownership status is not screened, from sanctioned jurisdictions, or with funds linked to criminal or terrorist-finance activity; failure to file a suspicious-transaction report with the Egyptian Money Laundering and Terrorist Financing Combating Unit (EMLCU), despite reporting obligations as a designated non-financial business or service provider.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Non-reporting and wilful AML breaches under Law No. 80 of 2002, as amended, are punishable by imprisonment of up to five years and a fine ranging from EGP 50,000 to EGP 500,000; repeat activity can result in confiscation of funds equal to the laundered value and revocation of the software vendor's permit to operate an Egyptian payment collection arrangement.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors and compliance officers who knew or should have known of the unlawful origin of funds are personally liable for fines and damages and may face criminal imprisonment. The EMLCU and public prosecutor may impose personal asset freezes and travel bans, and Egyptian AML law applies extraterritorially to Egyptian-managed cloud platforms that process the proceeds.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Collecting 10% dividend WHT or 20% royalty/interest WHT from counterparties or from shareholders' distributions but failing to remit the amounts to the Egyptian Tax Authority by the due dates, or diverting such public funds into operational accounts.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Withheld taxes are state money and non-remittance is treated as financial misappropriation. Law 91/2005 imposes a penalty of the higher of 100% of the withheld amount and the applicable monthly delay surcharge, plus criminal fines; persistent failure is punishable by imprisonment of not less than six months and not more than three years.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: The responsible director, tax manager, and board members may be made jointly and severally liable for the withheld amounts even after the LLC is liquidated; judges may issue stop-travel orders and asset attachment directly against the individual signatories. The corporate veil is pierced as a matter of statutory policy for collected-but-unremitted taxes.
